rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı contrasts pagans, who ranked other gods below Allah, with Christians, who make the three persons equal and unite them in a son.
rows.anchor: Nasârâ teslîsinde üçünü de müsâvî kılmışlar, bununla beraber üçünü de oğulda birleştirmişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two denials exclude God being either a parent or an offspring, including any derivation as a part from one or two prior sources; God is eternal, not originated.
rows.anchor: ne baba ne ana olmadığı gibi, ne tevellüd ne de tevâlüd suretiyle başkasından doğmadı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Begetting implies a finite, needy, imperfect parent, while a begotten being is originated and dependent, so neither can be the eternal necessary being.
rows.anchor: doğuran fâni ve muhtaç, eksikli olacağı gibi, doğan da kadîm, lizâtihî vâcibü’l-vücûd olmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is not generated in thought or knowledge either: he cannot be inferred from a prior major premise, first principle, proof, rule, or law.
rows.anchor: O vücudda başkasından doğmadığı gibi fikirde, marifette de doğurulmaz; bir kübrâdan, bir mebde’den istintac da edilmez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Created things and human meanings do not contain God as a logical implication; their origination and need instead proclaim their dependence and necessarily point to his existence, unity, and permanence.
rows.anchor: kendilerinden evvel ve kendileriyle beraber ve kendilerinden sonra O’nun varlığına ve birliğine ve bekāsına

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is manifestly discerned through everything yet remains hidden from direct knowledge through anything, since all things exist and are known through him.
rows.anchor: O her şeyden sezilir zâhir, hiçbir şeyle bilinmez bâtındır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God knows his own essence, and his knowledge is not a conceptual process that needs something to arise or be acquired; Jesus’s words illustrate this limit.
rows.anchor: ise ancak kendisi bilir ve ilmi de sudûr ve husûle muhtaç olacak fikir ve ta‘akkul kabîlinden değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first denial negates change and decay to affirm permanence; the second negates prior nonexistence and origination to affirm pre-eternity, which is conceptually prior to permanence.
rows.anchor: tegayyür ve fenâyı nefy ile bekāyı isbat

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since even polytheists did not deny God’s pre-eternity, denying begetting was more urgent; the unbegotten denial follows as evidence because the two are ordinarily linked.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ’nın kıdemi müşriklerce de inkâr edilmediği cihetle evvelâ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order also answers Christian hierarchy: they assert the Father first and Son second, so the negation of fatherhood precedes the negation of sonship.
rows.anchor: Nasârâ teslîsinde de evvelâ baba ilâh, sâniyen oğul ilâh iddia ettikleri

rows.speaker: Âlûsî
rows.claim: Alusi reports Christians’ creed as three distinguished hypostases: Father, Son, and Spirit, all sharing divinity while assigned different substances and relations; they identify them with necessary existence, intellect or knowledge, and will or love.
rows.anchor: Âlûsî Nasârânın kendi kitaplarında teslis akīdesini nasıl tasvir ettiklerini naklederek der ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reported Christians say the doctrine exceeds ordinary human understanding but must be believed, claiming to have received its names and teaching from the Apostles.
rows.anchor: tavr-ı beşeriyetin fevkinde ise de bunların hepsine iman vâcibdir

rows.speaker: Nasârâ
rows.claim: They explain the Son as proceeding from the Father’s intellect, receiving his entire divine nature and equal substance; they define generation as a living being proceeding from another living being in a way that shares its nature.
rows.anchor: Bu isimlerin ıtlâkının vechini beyan için de şöyle demişlerdir: ‘Çünkü uknûm-ı evvel bir menba‘ve mebde’ menzilesindedir

rows.speaker: Nasârâ
rows.claim: They call the Son the Word because he is said to be generated by the Father’s act of intellect, which they describe as the mind’s conception and speech.
rows.anchor: kelime aklın mefhûmiyeti ve nutkudur

rows.speaker: Nasârâ
rows.claim: They call the Son Wisdom because he is said to be generated from the Father through divine intellect.
rows.anchor: Baba’dan ilâhî aklının fiili ile doğmuştur, o ise hikmettir

rows.speaker: Nasârâ
rows.claim: They call the Son Light, Ray, or Radiance because wisdom reveals knowledge of realities wherever it is present.
rows.anchor: hikmet her nerede bulunursa onunla eşyânın hakāyıkına marifet ve nûr ve ziyâ

rows.speaker: Nasârâ
rows.claim: They say the Holy Spirit proceeds from the one will of Father and Son as divine love; although all three share spiritual nature, the relational titles Father and Son leave the common title Spirit for the third.
rows.anchor: Üçüncüye ‘Rûhu’l-kudüs’ denilmesi ise: Çünkü o baba ile oğuldan ikisinin bir olan irade fiiliyle sâdır olmuş

rows.speaker: Nasârâ
rows.claim: They distinguish the Spirit from the Son because the Spirit is said to proceed through will rather than the active intellect that would entail likeness to its agent.
rows.anchor: akl-ı fi‘lî ile sâdır olmamış, irade fiili ile sâdır olmuştur

rows.speaker: Nasârâ
rows.claim: They compare the first, second, and third hypostases to Adam, Abel, and Eve: one reality, though Abel is called a son and not a daughter.
rows.anchor: evvelden sânî, Âdem’den Hâbil gibi, sâlis de ondan Havvâ gibidir

rows.speaker: Nasârâ
rows.claim: They call the Spirit an agitator because he was ready to stir the Apostles after the Messiah’s absence.
rows.anchor: Havâriyyûna gelip de Mesih aleyhisselâm’ın fıkdânından dolayı onları kışkırtmaya müheyyâ bulunuyordu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says agency and passivity are not real relations in God as they are among created beings; the Christians nevertheless claim the three hypostases equal in essence, worship-worthiness, and virtue.
rows.anchor: Fâiliyet ve mef‘ûliyete gelince: Bunlar hakikaten mevcud değildirler

rows.speaker: Nasârâ
rows.claim: They claim the Word became incarnate through the Holy Spirit and united with Mary’s noblest blood, making Christ fully divine and fully human with two natures and wills while the Word remains simple and unchanged.
rows.anchor: Uknûm-ı sânî olan kelime tecessüd edip Rûhu’l-kudüs kuvvetiyle Meryem-i Betûl’ün kanından eşref-i eczâsıyla ittihad eylemiş

rows.speaker: Nasârâ
rows.claim: They cite Jesus’s bread and wine saying to claim that consuming his flesh and blood unites believers with him, as he is united with the Father.
rows.anchor: Mesih bir gün Havâriyyûna bir ekmek yedirdi ve bir şarab içirdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı cites Qur’anic passages rejecting claims that Jews and Christians are God’s children, that Christ is God, that God is one of three, or that God took a son without knowledge.
rows.anchor: bunların butlânı hakkında Kur’an’da ezcümle Sûre-i Mâide’de

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says Christians treat calling Allah the Messiah as equivalent to saying the Messiah is his son, so Qur’anic attributions need not be assigned to separate Christian sects.
rows.anchor: her birini onlardan bir mezhebin kavline tahsis etmeye hâcet yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allah is the eternal first source whose existence is necessary in himself; because everything else depends on him, divinity belongs to him alone.
rows.anchor: hiçbir şeyden sâdır olmamış, vücûdu lizâtihî vâcib mebde’-i evvel ezelî bir Zât-ı Hak vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge, will, and power are eternal attributes subsisting in the one divine essence, not separate persons or gods; Elmalılı rejects the Christian treatment of them as generated persons.
rows.anchor: İlim, irade, kudret birer zât değil O’nun bir olan zâtıyla kāim ezelî sıfatlarından ibaret olmak iktizâ eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He argues that the Trinity combines contradictions by making the divine persons simultaneously generated and ungenerated, one and three, distinct and united, then demands belief in Jesus’s divinity as a mystery.
rows.anchor: sâdır değil iken sâdır, sâdır iken gayr-i sâdır, bir iken üç, üç iken bir olmak gibi türlü tenakuzlarla dolu bir teslis

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not comprehending God’s essence differs from recognizing an explicit impossibility: reason can grasp the contradiction and judge it impossible.
rows.anchor: akıl, ermiyor değil, ermiş, mümteni‘tenakuz olduğunu ihâta ederek imtinâ‘ına hükmetmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To avoid defining or limiting God’s essence, one should contemplate his created works, blessings, signs, and attributes instead of trying to comprehend the essence itself.
rows.anchor: O’nun mahlûkātı, masnû‘âtı, eltâfı, nimetleri ile tecellî eden âyâtını, sıfâtını düşününüz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an refutes attributing the Trinity to God and Jesus, removes doubts, and guides people to unity through clear signs, especially the Throne Verse; this surah then condenses the proof.
rows.anchor: bâhusus Âyete’l-Kürsî’de ulüvv ü azamet-i ilâhiyeyi en beliğ bir beyan ile tebliğ ve tefhim eylemiş olduğu gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı links the opening denial of begetting to Qur’anic accusations that God begot, and places denial of fatherhood first to refute the first Christian hypostasis.
rows.anchor: diye vâki‘olan isnadlarını sarâhaten reddetmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Begetting would require a distinct part to separate from within and emerge outside, but God has neither parts nor an exterior; his knowledge and attributes are eternal, not generated persons, and his acts are creation.
rows.anchor: doğurmak bir şeyin dâhilinden hâricine mütemâyiz bir cüz’ün infisal ve hurûcuna mahal olmaktır, Allah’ın ise ne cüz’ü ne de hârici yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No being in metaphysical, natural, spiritual, or material realms can be God’s offspring; angels, spirits, jinn, or humans such as Adam and Jesus are created, and spirit itself is God’s command and creation.
rows.anchor: rûh da Allah’tan doğmuş değil, O’nun emri, mahlûkudur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God is not a father, the Father hypostasis cannot be God; the Son and Spirit claims fail with it, and Jesus, angels, intellect, and spirit are creatures rather than gods.
rows.anchor: Nasârâ teslîsinin birinci uknûmu babadır, Allah ise baba değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı raises whether denying that God begets also proves that a being begotten by someone else cannot be divine, since an offspring might seem more perfect than its parent.
rows.anchor: başkasından doğmuş herhangi bir veledden de mutlaka ulûhiyetin nefyi lâzım gelir mi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added denial rules out a begotten being as divine: however developed, it began in nonexistence, depends on its begetter, and cannot be fully self-sufficient or samad.
rows.anchor: doğurulmuş olan oğul veya kız herhangi bir veled doğurmamış olsa bile ilâh olamaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An imperfect source can produce a living being from the dead or life from soil only because God creates it; the result’s perfection is created and contingent, not divine by essence.
rows.anchor: ölüden diri, topraktan zîhayat yaratır, çıkartır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Christian Son or Word cannot be God because he is said to be begotten, and Jesus is likewise not God because he was born of Mary and shared ordinary bodily needs with her.
rows.anchor: Anası da kendisi de hem yemek yer hem çıkarırlardı

rows.speaker: Nasârâ
rows.claim: Elmalılı rejects their claim that the Son was eternally begotten by the Father at equal eternity: it makes the Son eternally dependent, and a dependent being has a servant’s rather than divine nature.
rows.anchor: Böyle demek biri diğerine ezelden muhtaç demekten başka bir şey değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the Son eternally begotten and equally eternal is contradictory: a generated being cannot equal its begetter in every respect or in pre-eternity, and a procession from one to two implies transition and sequence.
rows.anchor: Birden ikiye geçmek tasavvuru bir hareket demek olan bir intikal mânasını tazammun eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No equal can precede God as begetter or follow him as offspring; nothing equals him in essence, attributes, rank, likeness, opposition, or partnership, and no later contingent being could become his equal.
rows.anchor: ne evvelinde doğuran bir sâbıkı, mâfevki ne de âhirinde doğmuş, doğacak bir lâhıkı, mâtahtı olmadığı gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The world cannot be God’s equal: he existed before creating it, remains near to all things, and survives their passing away; several Qur’anic verses express this relation.
rows.anchor: yokken O var, onları yarattıktan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith saying Allah existed with nothing alongside him and remains as he was teaches that no equal could appear later if none existed with him eternally.
rows.anchor: Allah vardı ve onunla beraber bir şey yoktu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All created things may have a pair, equal, opposite, or likeness, as the verse about creating pairs indicates; Allah alone has no counterpart.
rows.anchor: Her şeyin bir beraberi, bir eşi, zıddı veya misli, bir nazîri, bir küfvü olabilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting kufuwan and then the pronoun for God emphasizes that denying an equal is the verse’s central point; the ordinary grammatical order could have been different.
rows.anchor: bu mânanın döküldüğü merkez noktası ise bu zarftır

rows.speaker: Sâhib-Keşşâf
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains that the adverbial phrase is fronted despite ordinary Arabic delaying such a phrase because it is the central object of emphasis.
rows.anchor: Sîbeveyh bunu kitabında tansis etmiştir

rows.speaker: Ebû Hayyân
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says the pronoun referring to Allah is fronted for emphasis.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ’ya râci‘olmasından dolayı ihtimam için takdim olunduğunu söylemiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction also suggests that an equal belonging to God is impossible by virtue of necessary existence and uniqueness; the denial concerns a rival to God, not every conceivable kind of equivalence among creatures.
rows.anchor: vücûd-i vâcibin, ehadiyetin iktizâ ettiği mümteni‘küfüv, kendinin küfvüdür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All forms of shirk are false, including pantheistic identification of God with the world, dualism’s two opposing creators, and the Christian claim that three equal hypostases form one God.
rows.anchor: Bir Allah var hiçbir vechile bir küfvü yoktur. O’ndan berisi hep mahluktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The readings vary in the final consonant and vowel of kufuwan: most read it with hamza, some with a silent fā and hamza, while Hafs reads final wāw; these are lexical forms of one word.
rows.anchor: Hafs’tan mâ‘adâ kıraatlerin hepsinde âhiri hemze ile كُفُوًا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kufuwan means something equal in rank or standing, a counterpart or peer; the Arabic spelling and pronunciation vary across related forms.
rows.anchor: şeye denir ki misil ve nazîr

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In its primary sense, two kufu counterparts independently possess equal worth and can fully replace each other; agreement permits joint action, but conflict makes their powers cancel, a relation called takāfuʾ.
rows.anchor: yekdiğerinden müstağnî olarak birbirinin makāmına tamamen kāim olacak haysiyette kâfi, mu‘âdil olmasıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This primary sense includes both an equal partner and an equal rival or opponent; males can match males and females females, but a male and female cannot match in this sense.
rows.anchor: aynı zamanda zıt, müsâvî rakib ve mu‘ârız mânasını da tazammun eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second sense means complementary counterparts of different but corresponding value, neither replaceable by the other, whose union is needed; this is the sense of marital compatibility.
rows.anchor: maksadın husûlü için ikisinin de tam kıymetleriyle ictimâ‘ı, izdivâcı şart olmaktır

rows.speaker: Râgıb
rows.claim: Raghib connects the root to rank and worth, cloth pieces joined at a room’s back, matching in marriage or war, reciprocal action, opposition, reversal, and poetic ikfā.
rows.anchor: كفأ، كفو kadr ü menzilettedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı lists Turkish equivalents such as equal, peer, mate, and companion; Kāmûs’s bektaş is no longer understood in that sense, while Azeris still use dadaş.
rows.anchor: “beraber”, “müsâvî”, “mu‘âdil”, “denk”, “eş”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because negative ahad means none and exhaustively denies things collectively and individually, God has no equal in any sense, including marital pairing; negating only a consort would not fully express uniqueness.
rows.anchor: “ehad” de “hiçbir” demek olarak gerek müctemi‘an gerek münferiden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An equal creator would need cooperation, noninterference, or the removal of its rival; perfectly equal powers instead cancel each other and cannot move even a straw, so neither could be divine.
rows.anchor: Bir noktayı tahrik için müsâvî iki kuvvet mütekābilen tatbik edildiği zaman müsbet menfî yekdiğerinin tesirini ibtal ettiği için hareket mümkin olmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the proof of mutual prevention: the Qur’an says multiple gods would corrupt heaven and earth or seek a way against the Lord of the Throne; only God is the self-sufficient, unconquerable ruler.
rows.anchor: buna “burhân-ı temânu‘” denilir ki Sûre-i Enbiyâ’da

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As supreme beauty and perfection, God has no counterpart, cannot change or perish, is sufficient for love and belovedness, and cannot be fully manifested to creatures without overwhelming them.
rows.anchor: asla infi‘âl ve tegayyürü, zeval ve fenâyı kābil olmayan ve hüsn ü cemâlin lâzımı olan sevmek sevilmek için de kendi kendine kâfi bulunan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’s request to see God is answered by a manifestation that crushes the mountain and leaves Moses unconscious; Elmalılı contrasts this with the misfortune of worshipping bounded idols that have many likenesses.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Mûsâ’ya “len terânî” buyurmuş, sonra da

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı summarizes the surah as a command followed by five propositions: Allah’s unknowable identity and oneness, his complete self-sufficiency as source and goal, and the denial of generation, offspring, and any equal or partner.
rows.anchor: dört âyet içinde gayet sade fakat derin ve muhît bir vecâzet ve belâgatle ma‘ârif-i ilâhiye ve akāid-i İslâmiye tafsîlâtının bütün esasını ihtivâ etmektedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concluding synthesis says all beings are created, nothing arises from God by generation, no being above, below, or alongside him can be divine, and claims of partnership or procreative Trinity are false.
rows.anchor: lizâtihî hakkın mukabili lizâtihî bâtıl ve mümteni‘olduğu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah repeats ahad at its opening and closing pauses to show its two Arabic uses: in affirmation it restricts, while in negation it generalizes, so the repetition is rhetorically meaningful.
rows.anchor: iki sûret-i isti‘mâlinin ikisine de tenbih olunmuştur
